episodes.description: In this episode, Jessica Regan, founder and CEO of FoodMesh, shares her mission to tackle one of Canada’s most pressing issues: food waste. With nearly half of the country's food going to waste while one in four Canadians faces food insecurity, Jessica built FoodMesh as a matchmaking platform that redirects unsellable but still good food to charities, farmers, and upcyclers. What began as a connector service has evolved into a full-scale B Corp, working with major grocers, municipalities, and over 2,500 organizations. Jessica also opens up about the challenges of building a mission-driven company, including fundraising while pregnant, navigating team dynamics, and creating a values-based culture. Maria discusses how she recognized the signs of burnout in herself and the steps she took to recover, both emotionally and physically. Through that process, she found a deeper calling to help others do the same. We also talk about the realities of building a values-driven business that prioritizes people over perfection. Maria shares how she built her practice with compassion at the core, creating a space where clients feel seen, heard, and supported. She emphasizes the need for boundaries, rest, and sustainable self-care, not just as trendy wellness buzzwords, but as foundational tools for long-term health. Throughout the episode, Måççaria offers practical insights and gentle reminders, encouraging listeners to reconnect with themselves, honor their limits, and permit themselves to heal. episodes.description: In this episode of The People-Driven CEO Podcast, host Shane Jeremy James, also known as S1H, speaks with Nik Vassev, the founder of NovoBeing. This VR therapeutics company integrates meditation, breathwork, and mental wellness into the healthcare system through the use of immersive technology. Nik discusses how he raised over $1 million in funding, overcame more than 300 investor rejections, and built a company supported by clinical trials that demonstrate real results, including a reduction in pain by over 50% with just 10 minutes of daily practice. Shane and Nik explore what it takes to lead a people-first startup in an environment that often promotes burnout. They cover important topics such as learning to delegate and trust your team, avoiding hustle culture, and safeguarding your health as a founder. If you are serious about building a purpose-driven business that can scale without compromising the well-being of your team or your sanity, this conversation is for you. episodes.title: Episode 37: From Corporate to Craft: Zahir Rajani on Reviving Family Legacy in Luxury Tailoring
episodes.description: In this episode, Shane Jeremy James, known simply as S1H, sits down with Zahir Rajani, the brilliant mind behind The Sartorial Shop, one of Vancouver’s most refined custom suit boutiques. Zahir didn't start in fashion; he originally came from the world of commercial real estate, where he held a stable job focused on buildings and contracts. However, he felt a deep desire to revive something more meaningful: his family’s legacy. His parents opened their tailoring shop back in 1984, following in the footsteps of Zahir’s grandfather, a master clothier in East Africa. Trading predictability for passion, Zahir took the leap into entrepreneurship, modernizing the family business and embracing the challenges that come with it. During their conversation, Zahir and Shane discuss the thrilling journey of being a founder—the steep learning curve, the pressure of leadership, and the continuous decisions regarding what to delegate and what to handle personally. They also explore the intersection of tradition and innovation, as Zahir integrates cutting-edge technology into the centuries-old craft of tailoring. His ambition? To make The Sartorial Shop the premier destination for luxury custom suits in Canada, and eventually, to expand that vision globally.
